title: Antevāsi spatial ic and the distinct pupil-agent history
predecessor_review: PG637 closed one MW/Vasu/PWG antevāsi pupil-state adverb interface while retaining PWG perhaps-neuter and inner antevāsa/aluk as Open. The Haim Dhundika passage now gives a positive spatial antevāsi tiṣṭhati construction and explicitly contrasts the person noun antevāsī guroḥ. The old pupil-state meaning/source units are not recredited.
tradition: Haim/Hemacandra source channel kept distinct from MW/PWG pupil-state wording

frames.meaning: a place in which residence is at the end/inside limit

contrast_control.note: This root-derived person channel is evidence for nonidentity; it is not copied into spatial antevāsi.

records: vāsa is nominal residence, not a sounded finite root form
antevāsi modifies tiṣṭhati as the fixed place/action expression
antevāsī guroḥ is the distinct resident/pupil agent noun
spatial antevāsi is licensed with tiṣṭhati
outer ic/i is retained as its own construction
no nominal case ending is assigned to the fixed adverb
spatial antevāsi has no root/pada/voice owner
Haim vas999 belongs only to contrasted antevāsī person formation

source_observations: Dhundika page248 positively distinguishes antevāsi tiṣṭhati spatial ic from antevāsī guroḥ root-derived person

source_policy.adopted: Admit the Haim spatial ante+vāsa+ic antevāsi reading and use the same passage to keep root999/ṇin antevāsī as a separate person channel.
source_policy.boundary: Do not replace PG637 pupil-state wording with this spatial gloss, assign vas999 to the adverb, or infer a universal neuter declension.
